<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults in `.targets` override project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–11  
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```
**Problem:** `.targets` is imported **after** the project file. These are unconditional assignments, so they **silently override** any project-level values. LibB sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` on line 13, but the `.targets` file stomps it back to `true`. The project author has no way to opt out.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```
This sets defaults that individual projects can override.

### 3. `LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwritten instead of appended
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 13–15  
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```
**Problem:** Two issues here:
1. **Overwrite:** This replaces `DefineConstants` entirely, killing SDK defaults like `DEBUG` and `TRACE`. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` will silently stop compiling in Debug builds.
2. **Unquoted condition:** `$(Configuration) == Debug` should have quotes around both sides. Without quotes, if `$(Configuration)` is empty, MSBuild evaluates ` == Debug` which is an evaluation error in strict mode and unreliable behavior.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
  <DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 4. `LibA.csproj` — Publish-on-build re-invokes the project, causing double-build and file races
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45  
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```
**Problem:** The `<MSBuild>` task call re-enters this project with an additional global property (`_IsPublishing=true`), which MSBuild treats as a **distinct project instance**. This means:
- The project builds **twice** (once for Build, once for Publish), doubling build time.
- Both instances write to the same `OutputPath` and `IntermediateOutputPath`, creating **file write races** that cause intermittent build failures.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` within the same project instance:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishOnBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" DependsOnTargets="Publish"
        Condition="'$(PublishOnBuild)' == 'true'" />
```
Or, for .NET 8+, simply set `<PublishAfterBuild>true</PublishAfterBuild>`.

### 5. `BrokenOrder.fsproj` — F# source file ordering is wrong
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 6–10  
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```
**Problem:** In F#, **compilation order matters** — files are compiled top-to-bottom as listed. `Services.fs` has `open BrokenOrder.Domain`, but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* `Services.fs`. This will fail with `FS0039: The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`.

Compare with the working `OrderService.fsproj` which correctly orders Domain → Services → Program.

**Fix:**
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 6. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package missing `PrivateAssets`
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 16–18  
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```
**Problem:** Analyzer packages should never flow to downstream consumers. Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, any project that references LibA or LibB via NuGet will **inherit the StyleCop analyzer**, forcing the analyzer on consumers who didn't opt in.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

### 7. `LibA.csproj` — Hardcoded Windows-specific `OutputPath`
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 7–8  
```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
```
**Problem:** This is an absolute Windows path. It will fail or produce unexpected results on Linux/macOS CI. It also bypasses the SDK's convention of `bin/$(Configuration)/$(TargetFramework)/`, breaking the standard layout and potentially causing bin/obj clash issues.

**Fix:** Remove it entirely (use SDK defaults), or use a relative cross-platform path:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\artifacts\LibA\</OutputPath>
```

### 8. `LibB.csproj` — Same hardcoded `OutputPath` issue
**File:** `LibB/LibB.csproj`, line 7  
```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```
**Problem:** Same as finding #7. Hardcoded absolute Windows path.

### 9. `LibA.csproj` — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath instead of PackageReference
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–30  
```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```
**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style assembly reference pointing to a `packages\` folder. SDK-style projects should use `<PackageReference>`. The hardcoded HintPath also targets `net6.0` while the project targets `net8.0` — the wrong TFM assembly is being used.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 10. `LibA.csproj` — Redundant `<Compile Include>` duplicates SDK auto-glob
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 21–24  
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```
**Problem:** The SDK automatically includes all `*.cs` files. The explicit `<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />` creates a **duplicate** Compile item, which will trigger `CS2002: Source file 'Class1.cs' specified multiple times`. The `Update` in the same ItemGroup as the `Include` also has subtle evaluation-order issues.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 11. `LibA.csproj` — Custom target missing `Inputs`/`Outputs` (breaks incremental builds)
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 32–34  
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```
**Problem:** This target has no `Inputs`/`Outputs` attributes, so it runs on **every build** regardless of whether anything changed. While this particular target is cheap, it's an anti-pattern — targets should declare incrementality.

**Fix:** If the target truly should run every time, add a comment documenting that intent. Otherwise, add `Inputs`/`Outputs`:
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Inputs="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)"
        Outputs="$(IntermediateOutputPath)version.marker">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
  <Touch Files="$(IntermediateOutputPath)version.marker" AlwaysCreate="true" />
</Target>
```
